clue.text: Unadorned, Richard's discarded stiff belt

parts.note: unadorned means bald, plain and bare

indicators.note: discarded tells us one word is thrown out of the name before it

parts.note: the name Richard; the 's stands for 'has'
stiff means hard, rigid

explanation.surface: A plain, unadorned Richard has given up wearing his stiff leather belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Richard's discarded stiff' reads as 'Richard has discarded HARD', leaving RIC after BALD. 'stiff belt' looks like one phrase, but only 'belt' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a sash worn over the shoulder to carry a sword, a kind of belt.

clue.text: Hurry, padding along behind

explanation.surface: Rushing about with padding along behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush about busily; also a frame or pad worn under a skirt to puff it out at the back.

clue.text: Drops out as result of this breach of security?

definitions.text: Drops out as result of this breach of security?

parts.words: Drops out as result of this breach of security?
parts.note: drops of liquid escape through a hole; secret information also escapes through a breach

explanation.surface: Agents drop out of an operation after a security breach.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid escaping through a hole is a seepage, and secrets escaping to the press are one too.

clue.text: Fabric — smart under picture

indicators.note: in a down answer under means placed after the first piece

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used in upholstery
to smart is to feel stung, to resent

explanation.surface: A smart fabric hanging beneath a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts RESENT below REP in this down answer; 'smart' looks like an adjective describing the fabric but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict something is to show it in a picture.

clue.text: Corot isn't as funny as these artists

indicators.note: funny suggests the letters of the phrase are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: Jean-Baptiste Corot is a landscape painter, not as comic as caricaturists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges CO ROT ISNT AS; 'these artists' are the ones who are funny, hence an apt definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These draughtsmen draw comic strips and caricatures.

clue.text: Produce light without gas conversion in city

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the glowing word wraps around the shuffled gas

parts.note: to produce light is to glow

indicators.note: conversion signals that the letters of gas are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A city lit without gas once electricity arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: GLOW is wrapped round ASG, the anagram of 'gas' signalled by 'conversion', giving GL-ASG-OW.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city.

clue.text: Anchor man

explanation.surface: A news anchor introduced as a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or chain that steadies a tent or mast; and a fellow or chap.

clue.text: Half-time servant in foreign capital

parts.note: the morning, written a.m., is one half of the day's time
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A servant takes half-time break in a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-time' suggests a match interval, but it is the first half of a twelve-hour clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Amman is the capital city of Jordan.

clue.text: Seating arranged amongst the shrubbery

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of seating are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Garden seats set out among the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amongst the' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Genista is the broom genus of flowering bushes.

clue.text: Outcome of military engagement abroad?

parts.note: the engagement is not a battle but a betrothal made while a soldier serves overseas

explanation.surface: The aftermath of an overseas battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who marries a serviceman met during a conflict abroad, the betrothal being an engagement.

clue.text: Do without females in group of speculators

explanation.surface: An all-male gathering of stock-market speculators.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag is a speculator who applies for new shares to sell them quickly at a profit, so a party of them is literally a group of speculators.
explanation.definitionFit: A men-only celebration before a wedding is a do with no women; and a gathering of share-flippers, called stags, is such a party.

clue.text: Kind pronouncement for House of Lords

indicators.note: pronouncement tells us a word is spoken aloud and we write down a word that sounds the same

parts.note: kind as a noun, a sort or manner

explanation.surface: A gracious statement made on behalf of the upper chamber of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House of Lords' is not Parliament here but the house of a lord of the manor.
explanation.definitionFit: A country estate with its great house was the seat of a feudal lord.

clue.text: Don't take liberty

explanation.surface: Someone warned against taking liberties.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something is not to take it; leave also means permission or freedom, as in shore leave.

clue.text: One who co-ordinates a medium sort of rise

parts.note: an organ is a medium of communication, such as a party newspaper

indicators.note: sort of suggests the word rise is put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A coordinator explains a middling kind of pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' turns RISE into ISER, added after ORGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser arranges events and people so that they work together.

clue.text: Yield, and accept compromise

parts.note: to yield is to give way
to accept is to take

explanation.surface: Advice to give way and accept a compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual concession, each side yielding something to the other.

clue.text: Fly interminably in part of Australia?

definitions.text: Fly interminably in part of Australia?

parts.words: Fly interminably in part of Australia?
parts.note: to fly without ever touching down describes the name, and the doubled first word also names the remote Australian outback beyond settled country

explanation.surface: Flying on endlessly over the Australian interior.
explanation.walkthrough: Something that never comes down to earth flies interminably, and the doubled first word is the Australian name for the vast empty outback.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian outback, especially remote northern Queensland and the Northern Territory, is nicknamed with this phrase, also the island of Peter Pan.

clue.text: About to curtail broadcast of network

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: broadcast in its sense of scattered widely, so the letters of curtail are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A plan to cut back a broadcasting network's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'broadcast' turns CURTAIL into TICULAR after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticular means like a net, describing a meshwork of fibres or lines.

clue.text: Open-air lesson put in the shade

parts.note: out means outdoors, in the open air
a class is a lesson

explanation.surface: An outdoor lesson held under the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone so far they are eclipsed.

clue.text: Works on units as ordered, with poor result

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the works come after the rearranged letters
ordered tells us the letters of units and as are put into a new order

parts.note: a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A factory putting units together as instructed, and turning out poor work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is part of the fodder, not a link: 'ordered' turns UNITS AS into UNSATIS, and 'on' puts FACTORY after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that ends with a poor result is inadequate, not up to standard.

clue.text: City providing main support for so-called poet

indicators.note: in a down answer a support goes beneath, so this piece comes after

parts.note: Shakespeare is nicknamed the Swan of Avon, so a poet is so called a swan
the main is the open sea

explanation.surface: A city whose economy supports a famous poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan Thomas came from Swansea, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a city on the south coast of Wales.

clue.text: Revival which tribe rashly holds back

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read from right to left
holds tells us the answer is kept within the run of words

explanation.surface: A revival movement which a reckless tribe suppresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rashly' looks like an anagram signal for 'tribe', but the answer lies backwards across 'which tribe rashly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal or resurgence, literally being born again.

clue.text: Recess near end of Parliament

parts.note: close means near

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of Parliament

explanation.surface: The recess near the end of a Parliamentary session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' suggests a holiday of Parliament, but it is a small room or cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard set in a wall is a small enclosed nook.

clue.text: Beaten and driven off without its backing

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the chasing word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to drive off is to chase away

indicators.note: backing means the word its is read from back to front

explanation.surface: Something beaten and driven away without support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ITS into STI, which 'without' (meaning outside) puts inside CHASED: CHA-STI-SED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be chastised is to be punished, originally by thrashing.

clue.text: Go a little way to have a meeting

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try
ST is the abbreviation for street, a little way along town

explanation.surface: Walking a short distance to meet someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a lovers' secret rendezvous.

clue.text: Intrigue a ministerial group

explanation.surface: Plotting by members of the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret faction plotting together; also the name given to Charles II's inner council of five ministers.

clue.text: Test silver or copper coin, for example

parts.note: the as was a Roman coin of copper or bronze
say means for example, as in 'take, say, a dozen'

explanation.surface: Testing whether a coin is silver or copper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is just a link between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay a metal is to analyse it for purity, as with precious metals like silver.

clue.text: Weapons ending up in baby's hands?

explanation.surface: Guns falling into the hands of a child.
explanation.walkthrough: A baby's hands are at the ends of its little limbs, so those limbs end up in hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and rifles are firearms carried by hand; and an infant's limbs are tiny, so they literally end in its hands.

clue.text: Possible result of love between partners

definitions.text: Possible result of love between partners

indicators.note: between puts the zero letter in the middle of the two partners

parts.note: in bridge the partners are North and South, abbreviated S and N
love is zero, the letter O, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A child may be the fruit of love between two partners.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy child is a possible offspring of a loving couple.

clue.text: Rigorous skill needed in bridge

indicators.note: in tells us the skill word sits inside the bridge word

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Bridge players need a rigorous technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game, but it is SPAN. 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and strict, like the harsh discipline of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: Hearing which can get listeners excited

parts.note: listeners are ears
hot means excited or agitated, as in hot under the collar

explanation.surface: A court hearing that can stir up the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Within hearing distance means within range of sound.
